comments.author: @cmw3737
comments.text: LLMs are the natural progression (possibly the end-point?) in the line of interpreters that take language that humans understand and write which result in computer programs. From machine code, to assembly language, to C to higher level language compilers, to query and scripting languages and DSLs, to no-code tools. The addition of function-calling is like the additional of functions to procedural languages. It enables a higher level of abstraction so the LLM itself can think in terms of blocks of functionality just like those old additions to compilers. I wonder if the next similar thing would  be module like behaviour where the LLM can re-use something in its memory reliably by 'solidifying' or freezing concepts that it creates. So you could prompt it to say now use that thing you just created to do this more complicated thing. If those 'things' could be somehow exported for use by other sessions then you'd get another exponential level of re-use.

It did get better over time, but it still kept trolling and doing dumb shit rather frequently.
